subject: maths
question: If a 16 metre long rope is stretched from the ground to the top of the house, such that the rope makes an angle of 30º with the ground, then find the height of the house.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 30°−60°−90° triangle, the side opposite to the 30° angle is always **half** of the **hypotenuse**.

Here, the **rope** acts as the **hypotenuse** (16 m) and the **house** is the side **opposite** to 30°.

Height of house = Hypotenuse ÷ 2

Height of house = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 metres.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the rope (Hypotenuse, AC) = 16 metres

Angle of elevation (θ) = 30°

**Formula Used:**

sin θ = Perpendicular (Height) ÷ Hypotenuse

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d24a190ecc6347fabfd94020182a73fc3667213ca5c53ce8c43d4f859ed29786.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ sin 30° = Height ÷ 16

⇒ 1/2 = Height ÷ 16

⇒ Height = 16 × (1/2)

⇒ Height = 8 metres

**∴ The correct answer is 8 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Standard values: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, and tan 30° = 1/√3.

30°−60°−90° Triangle Rule

The sides of such a triangle are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2, where 1 is opposite to 30° and 2 is the hypotenuse.

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking upwards at an object.</p
